human_notes: Update and tests agree (exact message given). Revised fix reads X.dtype before check_X_y, so a list or pandas DataFrame X now raises AttributeError instead of being validated; a robust fix would inspect np.asarray(X).dtype or guard with hasattr.
Minor: the revised __str__ docstring still says 'Use value when cast to str' while it returns the label (stale comment).

Tests only exercise keep_attrs=True, a subset of 'regardless of keep_attrs' (acceptable). Minor issues in the fix: docstring still says 'If True, keep the attrs of x', and attrs[0] is the first DataArray's attrs, so it is not cond's when cond is a plain array.
Plausibility is weak: Relational.as_set works over the reals, and a Complexes domain is ill-defined for inequalities. Still a coherent, testable change.
Edge case not covered by the update: explicit dtype=float16 is left as is (the fix converts only when dtype is None), which seems reasonable.

Update says any dimension name matching a sel keyword (e.g. method) must raise; fix hard-codes only 'method', so dims named 'tolerance' or 'drop' still collide. Tests only check 'method' with no message, so they match a subset. Comment line is mis-indented.

Requires DEFAULT_HASHING_ALGORITHM='legacy', but that setting names a hashlib algorithm: Django 3.1's security check (E100) allows only 'sha1'/'sha256', and signing uses the value as the digest, so 'legacy' would break signing elsewhere. Not a change a maintainer would plausibly make. Fix and tests implement the update literally.
Only changes the cosmetic ordering of imports in generated migrations (length-then-alphabetical instead of isort-style alphabetical); exact expected block is given, so tests match.

Forcing ProductSet.is_subset(FiniteSet) to False is mathematically wrong (the test asserts two equal sets are unequal via Eq(...).simplify() is S.false). The 'unless the FiniteSet is itself a ProductSet' clause is vacuous. The Eq check is not stated but follows from the is_subset rule.
Coherent but degenerate design: for coupled axes the result becomes NaN (which the test asserts). The update spells out the implementation.
Swapping the yielded tuple to (window, label) is an API-level change unrelated to the issue's 'center' bug; revised fix keeps the center fix and swaps the order.
Fix forces axis.grid(True) rather than 'leaving it enabled'; under the default Plot theme both readings pass the visibility test.
Revised tests only check the new message on an existing non-monotonic case; the duplicate-value case added by 'strictly' is not exercised (subset, acceptable).
Minor: revised get_annotation still infers 'default' but no longer uses it (dead code).

Only changes the sentinel string returned on OverflowError ('invalid' vs '0-0-0'); both lead to the same 'Enter a valid date' validation outcome, so effectively cosmetic. Exact value is given in the update.
Design keeps mode unchanged and adds text_mode, which leaves the youtube-dl symptom in the issue unresolved, but the update states this explicitly.

Minor: the fix raises only after set_output has already been applied to self and the other transformers, so the object is left partly configured; validating first would be cleaner. Exact message is given.
Deliberately drops PEP 415 handling, which is questionable but coherent for a debug view. Minor: the revised helper still computes suppress_context but never uses it (dead variable).
Presentation-only change: Literal values are rendered as monospaced literal nodes instead of plain text; both variants already avoid the spurious py:class xref.

Fix returns [] from find_ordering_name for any name ending in '_ptr', so the parent link adds no ORDER BY term at all instead of ordering by the parent's primary key. The test can pass on natural insertion order. The '_ptr' suffix check is also a string heuristic that would catch user fields with that suffix.
Tests check only the exception type, not the stated messages (subset, acceptable).

The update requires a fill_value parameter that is accepted but ignored. The parameter did not exist before the fix, so this adds dead API rather than keeping it for compatibility, and behaviour equals the pre-fix default. Revised fix does this literally but its docstring says fill_value replaces missing values (contradicts behaviour) and it leaves a stray whitespace-only line.
Only switches the xref role for None from 'obj' to 'data'; both resolve the Python None entry via intersphinx, so the user-visible effect is negligible.

Making is_fits return True for every non-None path would make the registry identify any file (e.g. .ecsv, .hdf5) as FITS, breaking format auto-detection; not a change a maintainer would plausibly make. Fix and tests implement it literally.

Revised fix replaces the original `del deconstruction[2]['to']` with the check, so 'to' stays in the relation-agnostic field definitions. That regresses renamed-model detection for any FK whose target is renamed. It also applies to every relation with remote_field.model, not only ForeignKey subclasses.
Tests check only the exception type, not the stated message (subset, acceptable).
Functionally implements warn-and-ignore, but the revised fix is sloppy: the null-mask block is duplicated verbatim and a comment is mis-indented. The behaviour is unaffected.
Dropping empty-string entries from LEVEL_TAGS has no observable effect on Message.level_tag, which already falls back to '' via .get(); only the dict contents change.

Weakly motivated change (bytes body turned into a mutable bytearray). Fix converts any bytes body, not only bytes passed as data=, so multipart bodies built from files= also become bytearray; this goes beyond the update.
